rewrite: Another track that really stands out for me is “Never Have to Say Goodbye.” We’re in Las Vegas. One of my friends, who was like a father to me, helped me get clean and sober a few years back—it’s no secret I’ve struggled with sobriety on and off. This guy truly reached out when I was at my lowest, helping me rebuild my life. But then, slipping back into old habits, I was out living that former life while he was in Vegas on vacation with friends. He had a heart attack and passed away. That hit me hard, man—like losing another father. I’d already lost one, not to death but to estrangement, and then Dan, this second father figure, was gone. It was a rough thing to go through. Years later, I’m in Vegas looking for inspiration to write, and as I said earlier, it felt laid out before me. Whenever I need to write a song, it becomes clear. I needed to make peace with Dan and say what I never told him. He’d call to check in, but I wouldn’t answer—I didn’t want him to see how badly I was doing. Now, approaching three years sober, I believe he’s looking down from heaven, smiling. I felt it was necessary to express my peace through music; putting things into a song gives me closure. I just want to make him proud. Waking up each day with a sober mind and clear head lets me be part of life’s flow, not its destruction—after years in that dark place, having clarity means everything.
